mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which increases wage pressures and prompts the Federal Reserve to raise rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals a demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 6-month MA AND HOUST > 6-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate profit growth and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of strong monetary easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes outside monetary easing periods.
